summary: Feature: Symmetric mirrors two lines, two arcs or two circles about any line, a construction line or the H or V axis, as one relation that stores the two curves and no pairing of their points. Lines pair an end they share with itself and otherwise pair their ends by where they are before each edit, so either line may run either way. A mirror reverses an arc's sweep, so arcs of one direction pair each start with the other's end and arcs of opposite directions pair start with start and end with end. Circles pair their centres, and mirrored arcs and circles keep one radius. The relation lowers every pair whole, as point mirrors: an end both curves share is held on the mirror, and circles add one equal-radius row. There is no new equation kind. The relation yields to the rest of the sketch. It lowers after every other relation, and each of its rows is a constraint of its own. A row that only repeats what the curves, fixed values or other relations already keep is solved but not reported as redundant; one that disagrees still conflicts. So two lines kept Horizontal mirror about V, and the freedom left counts only what the mirror adds. A mirror none of whose rows adds anything is redundant, and is refused like any other redundant relation. A pair that does not reflect yet starts the second curve’s point at the first’s image. So a new mirror moves the second curve onto the first, and arcs settle on the true mirror rather than on another crossing of their circles. A free mirror line turns to fit: of the pairings and lines the mirror can take, it starts from the one that moves the sketch least, counter-clockwise when two move it alike, and a failed solve tries the next, keeping the start of every other mirror that solved. Where a mirror starts never depends on the order the sketch stores its points, edges and relations. Points held by Fix, by expressions, by fixed distances or through Coincident never move, so a mirror lies on the perpendicular bisector of a held pair or turns about a held end, and pairs that a point Symmetric already mirrors stay paired. So a Horizontal and a Vertical line mirror about a free line drawn near upright, and held points that leave the mirror no line are refused as conflicting, naming the relations that hold them. A solve that could meet the mirror only by collapsing the curves is refused with the reason, and a start that would shrink a mirrored curve below a hundred-thousandth of its size before the edit is passed over for one that does not, and kept only where none does. The Constrain tool and the selection offers plan it through the shared planner. Two curves of one kind and a line or an axis, picked in any order, offer Symmetric; among three lines the one construction line is the mirror, or else the line picked last. Two kinds, and pairs a mirror cannot map, are refused with the reason. So are lines whose other relations or fixed ends keep them in directions the mirror cannot map, naming those relations; arcs or circles whose fixed radii differ; and point Symmetrics that pair two lines’ ends the other way round from where they lie. The relation is stored only in this form. Point Symmetrics that already hold two lines' ends, or a centre Symmetric of two circles with their Equal radius or both radii fixed alike, show as applied, and Remove removes them. Where other relations keep part of a mirror, such as one point Symmetric, an Equal or a shared end on the mirror, the curve Symmetric joins them. Equal on curves that already mirror is refused. Equal refuses a line with an arc or circle, with the reason. Marks sit on both curves and on the mirror line, and the relation list and inspection name it Symmetric curves. Trim removes a curve Symmetric with either curve it trims and lists it; Split and Extend refuse it while it names the curve.
warning: Potentially breaking for CAD files and agents. Installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions and controller output are not affected. The sketch graph schema gains a second Symmetric shape, { kind: 'symmetric', curveIds, lineId }. Sketches that store it do not open in 0.0.793 or earlier; the CAD format is alpha and carries no compatibility in either direction. Every relation a sketch stores today keeps its meaning and compiles to the same equations: the 0.0.788 equation baseline replays unchanged, byte for byte. Compiled equations gain an optional yields flag, which only a curve Symmetric’s rows carry. Only the TypeScript diagnosis reads it; the native buffers do not carry it. Two circles with a line, picked in the Constrain tool or offered for a selection, now give the curve Symmetric, which also keeps their radii equal. Before, they gave a point Symmetric of their centres. A point and a circle still give the point form, and three lines now also offer Symmetric. A Trim of a mirrored curve now lists the curve Symmetric in removedRelationIds. An agent request that confirms an older list rejects with unconfirmed-sketch-trim-removals and names the expected IDs. The relation editor's Symmetric centers checkbox still mirrors only two circles' centres, and does not show a curve Symmetric of those circles as checked. The worker protocol stays version 7.

checklist.schema: Sketch graph schema change: the symmetric relation gains a curveIds variant, two lines, two arcs or two circles mirrored about the lineId, which names a line or @h or @v. A parse refuses it with invalid-sketch-symmetry, giving the reason, for: two kinds; an axis among the curves; a mirror that is not a line; one curve twice; two circles on one centre; two lines on the same two ends; arcs on the same three points; arcs sharing an end that their directions pair with another point; a shared end off the mirror; and a curve point at an end of the axis line that the curves do not share. Its key sorts curveIds, so either order is one relation. Lowering emits only existing rows: symmetric-midpoint, symmetric-perpendicular, point-on-line for a shared end, and difference for two circles' radii. The lowering context gains each point’s position before the edit, its Coincident identity, start(pointId, position), held(pointId), startChoice(relationId, count), choose(costs), unmet(relationIds), mirrorTurn(firstLineId, secondLineId, mirrorId) and lineAngle(lineId). start sets the free coordinates of a point’s whole Coincident identity where the relation puts them, and the compiler applies those values before solving. held reads what keeps a point in place across its Coincident identity. mirrorTurn and lineAngle read the relation planner’s new mirrorTurn and lineAngle: the directions the relations and fixed ends that keep two lines’ directions force on a free mirror line, and the direction they keep one line in. The curve Symmetric searches a few starts with them (cadSketchMirrorStarts). compileCadSketchEquations takes an optional startChoices, the start each relation that offers several sets out from, and its result gains startChoices, each such relation with the movement of each of its starts, and unmet; the native attempt searches a failed stored solve’s further starts one connected component of parameters at a time (cadSketchNativeStartSearch), and reports a failure that names no relation as conflicting with the relations an unmet relation records. Relation definitions gain an optional yields. lowerAll lowers such relations after all the others, in graph order. Each of their equations takes a tag of its own and the equation model’s new optional yields flag; the TypeScript diagnosis reads that flag and reports such an equation as redundant only when every equation of its relation is, so a relation that adds nothing is refused as redundant. Only the curve Symmetric yields, so every other sketch compiles and diagnoses as before. The precision policy gains two roles. mirrorPairingTieRelative (1e-9): two lines pair their ends crossed only when that is nearer to each other's mirror images, in summed squared gaps, by more than that fraction, so near ties keep start with start; two starts of a curve mirror whose summed squared movements differ by at most that fraction tie too, and so do two combinations of the starts of mirrors whose parameters connect. mirrorCollapseRelative (1e-5): a solution that leaves a mirrored curve’s length or radius below that fraction of its size before the solve ranks below one that does not, so a native solve tries its other starts for one and keeps the first such solution only where none is found; the role refuses nothing. No existing role changes, so CAD_PRECISION_VERSION stays 1. A native solve that leaves a curve Symmetric’s curve or mirror line degenerate, as the graph checks report it, at or below minimumLengthMm, is rejected as failed with its own message instead of the generic invalid solution; other sketches report as before, and the graph checks are unchanged. No UPID, post, machine package, execution plan, saved revision, storage, journal, worker reply or native buffer protocol schema change. The native protocol stays version 7 with the same buffers, and the Rust solver and the committed WebAssembly module are unchanged. The post engine API remains 1 and the saved-job engine remains 3.
checklist.events: No execution event, input-version or cancellation change. Agent operand change: set-sketch-relation accepts the curveIds form of symmetric. cad_inspect_sketch_constraints names it Symmetric curves, with its own meaning, and lists every point of both curves and the axis line's ends. The relation offers and the Constrain tool give it for two curves of one kind and a line or an axis. Trim's removedRelationIds include a curve Symmetric that names the trimmed curve; Split refuses it with dependent-sketch-split, and Extend refuses it as a dependency. Nothing new runs on pointer moves. A lowering of a curve Symmetric reads the pairing once, which for two lines compares four distances, and the planner reads a selection once. Its direction and fixed-radius checks read the sketch’s relations once for each plan of two curves. A curve Symmetric whose mirror is not met yet weighs at most four starts while it lowers, asking the planner, cached for each sketch graph, for directions; a mirror already met weighs none and asks nothing, so re-solving or dragging a kept mirror does no more. Only a stored solve that fails retries, searching one connected component of mirrors at a time through at most 16 combinations of their starts, each one compile and one native solve: at most 1 + Σ (min(n_k, 16) − 1) solves, n_k being the product of the start counts in component k, so mirrors that share no parameters cost the sum of their starts, at most three further solves for each mirror of two lines. Arcs and circles have one start. Drags never retry, and offers and hover never compile or solve.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change, and no WebMCP tool added or removed. The symmetric agent summary names lines, arcs and circles, and the WebMCP discovery metadata stays at 51,178 of 51,200 bytes, unchanged. The public agent guide documents the curve form, its pairing, its refusals, the relations recognised as already holding it, the relations it joins and the ones it refuses by name, the free mirror’s turn from the start that moves the sketch least, about held points and keeping held pairs, keeping each mirror’s start that solved and alike in any stored order, whole-relation redundancy, the collapse refusal, starts that would shrink a mirrored curve passed over, the Equal refusals, and Trim, Split and Extend. The CAD guide documents picking, marks, arc pairing in both directions, mirroring two horizontal lines about V, the free mirror’s turn about held points and kept pairs, and refusals. Constrain offers Symmetric for two lines, two arcs or two circles and a line or an axis, in any order. Equal says why a line and an arc or circle cannot be equal.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change.

checklist.verification: Equation baseline: the 0.0.788 fixture replays unchanged and is not re-recorded. Every input gives the same compiled models, native answers, graph-check hashes, constraint inspection row hashes and solver attempts, byte for byte. For that, the point Symmetric keeps its recorded agent meaning; the curve form takes its own through a new optional meaningOf on relation definitions, which constraint inspection reads. New tests: cadSketchCurveSymmetry (17) covers nine scenes about the V axis, the H axis, a fixed construction line and a fixed ordinary line. The scenes are: lines; lines running opposite ways; lines sharing an end; arcs; arcs running opposite ways; arcs sharing an end, a centre, or both ends; and circles. For every scene, mirror and pick order it checks the offer and the Constrain tool step, and choosing the mirror among three lines. It also checks the prompts and the pairing, including opposite line directions, opposite arc sweeps, and the pairing tie on each side of mirrorPairingTieRelative. Lowering: every pair whole, after every other relation, each row a yielding constraint of its own: 4, 4, 3, 6, 6, 5, 5, 4 and 3 rows, with the circle radius row. Arcs remove one freedom fewer than their rows, as the second radius follows. A native solve checks the reflection and the freedom left. Mirror parity: 1,377 configurations, each compared three ways (H, the construction line and the line against V). They cover every choice of fixed, expression-held and Fix-held points, alone, beside an Equal or with a conflict planted 0.5 mm along the mirror. Lines are also squared to the mirror, one or both, and radii are fixed alike on A, on B or on both, alone or beside Equal. Every one agrees in result, reason, message, freedom, conflicting, redundant and partly redundant ids, issues and definition, across solved, redundant, conflicting and failed outcomes. The failed outcome is the lens whose ends collapse at a stall. Refusals cover two kinds, one curve twice, a mirror that is not a line, an axis among the curves, circles on one centre, lines on the same two ends, arcs on the same three points, arcs sharing a start, an axis line end, and Equal of a line with an arc or circle. De-duplication and recognition: key order; applied with Remove ids; point Symmetrics of two lines applied; circles with a centre Symmetric and an Equal radius applied; Equal refused on curves that mirror. Also covered: names and meanings, an agent edit with the curve form, Trim removing the relation from an end trim and a circle trim, and Split and Extend refusing it. Existing tests touched: the offers (three lines also offer Symmetric; two circles on one centre give the circles reason), the registry (a curve Symmetric reference), the constraint tool (the Equal and circles reasons), the glyph layout (curve marks on both curves and the mirror line, none for an axis), the offer parity rules, and the precision role pin. Mutations before review, each restored, against cadSketchCurveSymmetry, the offer parity, both baselines, the registry, offers, symmetry relations, lowering, constraint tool and glyph layout suites (96 tests). Arcs of one direction paired start with start fails 7. Two point Symmetrics no longer counted as a line mirror fails 1. A key that keeps the curves in stored order fails 2. Circles without their equal-radius row fail 2 (these four ran on the first lowering). The equation baseline passes under each. Trim without the curve Symmetric removal fails the trim test, and a pairing tie of 0 fails the pairing test and the precision pin. Merge: main at 0.0.791 is merged, keeping 0.0.794 after 0.0.793. The pairing tie reads the new precision role to satisfy the precision literal check. Since review round 1. (1) Arcs lowered their second end pair as one row chosen from the geometry, so a solve could settle on the other crossing of the arcs’ circles. In the repro, arcs about V both counter-clockwise, A with centre (20,10), start (25,10), end (20,15) and B with centre (-20,10), start (-20,15), end (-15,10), the solve settled on another branch instead of the true mirror. Every pair now lowers whole, so arcs give 6 rows for 5 freedoms; the rows yield, and a pair that does not reflect starts the second curve’s point at the first’s image. The repro solves to B’s end at (-25,10). A sweep covers 1,152 arc pairs: V or a fixed line; two centres; radii 3 and 6; starts at 0, 100, 190 and 280 degrees; sweeps of 60 and 200 degrees; both directions; c1 and s1 each free, expression-fixed or held by Fix; and A’s radius, B’s or neither fixed to 7. Each one solves to the true mirror (640) or is rejected (512); none solves anywhere else. (2) The mirror yields to the rest of the sketch, so two lines kept Horizontal mirror about V. The freedom left counts only what the mirror adds, and nothing is reported redundant that is not. The planner refuses lines whose directions the mirror cannot keep. When the mirror’s, A’s and B’s directions are all fixed, it compares 2θM − θA with θB modulo π within CAD_PRECISION.angularAccuracyRad. When Parallel, Perpendicular, Collinear, Horizontal or Vertical tie A to B, it compares their parity. The reason names the relations, for example: “The Horizontal and Vertical relations keep these lines in directions that cannot mirror about the V axis. Remove one of them first.” A matrix puts none, Horizontal or Vertical on each of A and B, about H, V, a free construction line drawn near V and a line fixed at 120 degrees. It gives 26 applied, 8 refused by name, and 2 the free line cannot reach from near V. Those 2 fail the graph check and are never solved wrongly; with the line drawn near the bisector, they solve with freedom 6. Removing the Horizontal or Vertical afterwards leaves the whole mirror with freedom 8 or 4, and nothing moves. Beside Parallel, Perpendicular or Collinear, Equal, point Symmetrics, holds on the H axis and a shared end on the mirror, each case solves with the exact freedom. Four direction conflicts are refused. (3) Fixed radii mirror when they are equal: a circle radius expression, a constant radius or diameter size, or an arc with its centre and an end fixed, on A, on B or on both. Circles keep freedom 2, arcs 4, and arcs fixed at two points each keep 0. When the fixed radii differ, the plan is refused with “These circles have fixed radii that differ, so they cannot mirror each other.” A sketch that stores the mirror anyway is rejected as conflicting, naming it. No general rule turns rows over only fixed parameters into checks. The mirror’s own rows of that kind yield, so they agree silently or conflict. A global rule would change the diagnosis of other relations and probably the baseline, so it was not added. (4) Where other relations keep part of a mirror, the curve Symmetric now joins them, so Equal is no longer skipped. The 11 cases are: half a line mirror, either way round; equal lines; both of those; a shared end on the mirror; equal circles; mirrored centres; mirrored arc centres; mirrored arc ends with equal arcs; equal arcs; and a shared arc end on the mirror. Each solves to the whole mirror with no redundancy. Equal on mirrored curves stays refused. Mutations, each restored, against cadSketchCurveSymmetry and the equation baseline (22 tests). The equation baseline passed under each. Arcs dropping one row of their last end pair fail 2. No seeding fails 2. The original defect, one row and no seeding, fails 4, including the repro. Rows that do not yield fail 7. Rows not deferred after other relations fail 2. No redundancy filter for yielding rows fails 6. No direction refusal fails 2. A circle radius row that does not yield fails 3. No fixed-radius refusal fails 1. Equal refused again in a partial mirror fails 2. The selectable-axes spec gains a test that draws two lines level with Create relations on, then makes them Symmetric about V from Constrain. Both Horizontal relations stay, B lands on A’s image, and the status reads Under defined · 3 DOF. Since review round 2. (1) A free mirror line about which one line is kept level and the other upright has to turn 45 degrees, and from near V the solver met the curves collapsed first. In the repro, Horizontal A from (10,5) to (25,5), Vertical B from (-10,5) to (-10,20) and a free construction line from (0.5,-60) to (-0.5,60), adding Symmetric returned an invalid solution. The planner’s new mirrorTurn reads the direction forced on a free mirror line whose class no relation anchors: half the sum of the lines’ directions where both are known, or a fixed turn from A’s direction where relations tie A to B. The lowering starts the mirror there before it seeds the pairs. Of the two directions, a quarter turn apart, it takes the one nearer the mirror’s own, turning counter-clockwise when both are 45 degrees away within CAD_PRECISION.angularAccuracyRad. It turns about an end that cannot move, that Fix holds or that the lines share, the start before the end, or else about its middle. Nothing turns where nothing forces it. The repro solves with freedom 6, no redundancy and the mirror at 135 degrees; A stays where it is and the mirror keeps its middle. A new test starts from that valid sketch and its swap: tilted left of V the mirror turns to 135 degrees, tilted right to 45, and exactly upright counter-clockwise to 135. Lines kept perpendicular, or parallel at 45 degrees, turn it to 135 and solve with freedom 7. The H/V matrix now gives 28 applied and 8 refused by name, with nothing unreached. A solve that leaves a curve Symmetric’s curve or mirror line degenerate is now rejected as failed with “Symmetric could only be met from here by collapsing the mirrored curves. Move the curves or the mirror line nearer to a mirror image first.” A test stores A level and B upright about a construction line whose ends Fixed x keeps on V: the planner refuses it by name, and stored anyway it is rejected with that message, listing both lines as degenerate. (2) Yielding hid a relation that adds nothing. In the repro, four free circles of radius 4 at (10,5), (-10,5), (-10,-5) and (10,-5), with A–B and C–D about V and B–C about H, adding D–A about H solved with freedom 3. Redundancy is now read for each relation. The rows of a yielding relation that adds at least one independent row may still yield. A relation none of whose rows adds anything is reported redundant and refused like any other, with the same diagnostic and the sketch unchanged. The chain stays on the solver path: the planner offers it, and the solver refuses it as redundant, naming it, with freedom 3. The open chain of three still solves with no redundancy. Mirrored centres with both radii fixed to 4 keep the whole mirror. The planner now counts radii fixed alike as held, so the plan shows as already applied, naming the centre Symmetric. A sketch that stores it anyway is refused as redundant. With one radius fixed, the mirror still adds the other and solves with freedom 2. (3) The CAD guide now says that arcs drawn the same way pair each start with the other’s end, and arcs drawn opposite ways pair start with start and end with end. Mutations, each restored, against cadSketchCurveSymmetry and the equation baseline (25 tests). The equation baseline passed under each. No per-relation aggregation fails 1, the redundancy test. No mirror turn fails 2, the matrix and the turn test. A tie that turns clockwise fails 1, the turn test. Turning to the farther direction fails the same 2. No collapse guard fails 1, the collapse test. Radii fixed alike not counted as held fails 1, the redundancy test. Follow-up for the diagnostics work (D1): a general rule that turns equations over only fixed values into checks, a pre-existing main issue, is not added here. Also for D1: canonical equation order by relation id for every sketch, which changes the equation baseline and so needs a deliberate baseline update there. Since review round 3. Each patch to the single-choice turn exposed another case, so the turn is replaced by a small candidate search, cadSketchMirrorStarts.ts; round 2’s turnedMirror and movable are removed. Pairs that relations lowered earlier keep about the same line, point Symmetrics or another curve Symmetric, are hard input: only a pairing that keeps them is a candidate. Each such pairing on each line the mirror can take is one: an axis, or a mirror whose ends are both held, stays; a free mirror lies on the perpendicular bisector of a pair held at two places, else through a held point at each direction the lines’ relations force or toward a second held point, else through a shared point or its own middle at each forced direction. A candidate that would move a held coordinate is dropped before any solve. What holds a point is read across its Coincident identity: expressions, Fix, fixed X or Y distances, a point on H or V, the origin and the axes. On a line the holds fix, a candidate is dropped too where a line both of whose ends held points settle would collapse or leave the direction its relations keep. Candidates are ordered by the summed squared movement of every point they start, the mirror’s ends included, then within mirrorPairingTieRelative by the larger counter-clockwise turn, then start with start. The solve starts from the first. A stored solve that is not solved recompiles and solves from each other in turn, taking the first that solves at its most certain without collapsing. Where the holds leave no candidate on any line the mirror could take, the relation records the relations that hold them, and a failure that names no relation is reported as conflicting with those, in graph order. The search runs only while lowering a mirror that is not met: a mirror that the nearest pairing already reflects about returns before any planner call, so re-solves and drags of a kept mirror do no more. Drags never retry, and offers and hover use only the planner. Two lines have at most four candidates, so a stored curve Symmetric whose mirror is not met adds at most three compiles and native solves; arcs and circles have one candidate. cad-performance.md records this. (1) The review’s repro, Horizontal A from (10,5) to (25,5), Vertical B from (-10,5) to (-10,20), a free mirror from (0,-60) to (0,60) and a point Symmetric of a1 and b1, solves with freedom 6 and the mirror at 45 degrees, b1 at a1’s image and B from (5,10) to (5,25). With the point Symmetric on a1 and b2 instead, B turns over to keep it. With A level above B upright, which alone turns the mirror to 135 degrees with B’s ends crossed, a point Symmetric of a1 and b1 keeps them straight at 45. Each offers only the kept pairing’s two starts, and the first solves. (2) All four ends held, A from (10,5) to (25,5) and B from (5,10) to (5,25), by Fix or by expressions, with the mirror free: the mirror takes their perpendicular bisector, y = x, and the sketch solves with freedom 2. (3) The H/V sketch with the mirror from (0.5,-60) to (-0.5,60), its start Coincident with a point whose expressions fix it at (0.5,-60): the mirror turns about that start to 45 degrees, A does not move, and B lands from (65.5,-50.5) to (65.5,-35.5), with freedom 4. The turn test now expects least movement. With A level and B upright the mirror turns to 45 degrees whether drawn left or right of V, and with A upright and B level to 135. A level above B upright about V, where 45 straight and 135 crossed move the sketch alike, turns counter-clockwise to 135 with B crossed. Each case checks B’s ends exactly. A held-position matrix of 216 configurations: lines already mirrored about y = x and lines apart, each alone and kept level and upright, arcs mirrored about y = x and circles apart, about a free mirror drawn on V, with each set of their points and the mirror’s start held by Fix, by expressions, by Coincident with an expression-fixed point, and by fixed X and Y distances. Each solves with nothing held moving and a clean graph check, or is refused naming relations, and the four holds give one answer. A conflict names every hold relation; expressions are not relations. The 9 refusals are listed: both ends of a line held make Horizontal or Vertical redundant (3, one beside a conflict), and held points that leave the mirror no line conflict with it (6), naming Horizontal and Vertical where they decide it. A retry test: lines sharing an end that Fix holds, kept parallel, mirror along them or square to them. Along them moves least but collapses both, so the second start solves, in two native solves. A met-gate test: a kept mirror compiled again or dragged offers no starts, seeds nothing and solves once; a drag of the sketch before it was mirrored solves once. Mutations, each restored, against cadSketchCurveSymmetry and the equation baseline (29 tests). The equation baseline passed under each. Ignoring the existing pairing fails 1, the repro test: the held pairing offers 4 starts instead of 2, and without that check the a1-onto-b2 sketch spends a solve that collapses B before the retry reaches the held pairing. Trying only the first candidate fails 1, the retry test. Dropping Coincident-identity immovability fails 2, the repro test and the held-position matrix. Since review round 4. (1) A retry reset every other mirror to its first start, so two copies of the retry sketch, each solving only from its own second start, were refused with the collapse message. The relations offering several starts are now grouped by the connected component of the parameters their equations touch, whatever start each takes (cadSketchNativeStartSearch.ts), as native solves each connected group alone. Only the components a failure names, through the diagnosis or the graph checks of the solved graph, are searched, each through its combinations least moved first, ties within mirrorPairingTieRelative going to the earlier relation’s earlier start, up to 16. A combination after which its component no longer fails is kept while the next component is searched. Where the failure names nothing, or a trial solution cannot be rebuilt into a graph to check, a combination is taken only if the whole sketch solves. With n_k the product of the start counts in component k, the worst case is 1 + Σ_k (min(n_k, 16) − 1) solves: the sum of the starts for disjoint mirrors, not the product. cad-performance.md records it. The two copies 100 mm apart now solve in three native solves with freedom 8, each copy as it solves alone, B folded out to (8,-12.5). With Parallel between their mirrors, the copies form one component, and the fourth combination, both second starts, solves with freedom 7. (2) A free mirror a quarter turn from the only direction its lines allow could turn either way, and a tilt of 1e-14 rad flipped the turn. A turn within the angular accuracy of −90 degrees now counts as +90, and the mirror’s ends follow the turned direction, so the counter-clockwise turn wins whichever way noise tilts it. The repro, Horizontal A from (0,1) to (2,1), Horizontal B from (0,1) to (-2,1) and a free construction mirror from (-2,0) to (2,0), solves tilted by −1e-14, 0 and +1e-14 rad to one answer: A and B stay, and the mirror runs from (0,-2) to (0,2), with freedom 6. Start costs tie through mirrorPairingTieRelative, and a movement within the driver tolerance counts as none. (3) Where two mirrors would start one curve, the one lowered last won, so the stored relation order changed the geometry. Every curve Symmetric is now planned together when the first lowers, in relation-id order, keeping the pairs of point Symmetrics, read in id order too, and of the mirrors before it; where two would start one point, the one whose id sorts last starts it. held reads relations in id order. The context’s paired and partners are removed; choose takes each start’s movement, and startChoice reads the start a retry asks for. The repro, A from (10,5) to (25,5), B from (5,10) to (5,25), C from (30,7) to (12,15), a free mirror from (0,-60) to (0,60), and curve Symmetrics A–B and C–B, compiles the same starts point by point and solves to one answer within 1e-9, with freedom 8, with the relations in either order and with points and edges reversed. The rest of the seeding and candidate path was checked for order. The shared direction planner anchors a class of lines on its first line with fixed ends, which consistent sketches agree on within roundoff. The solver itself still receives equations in graph order, so its path, and in rare sketches the solution it reaches, can still depend on stored order. New tests: the two failing copies apart (three solves) and with parallel mirrors (one component, four solves), the combination order and cap, both tilts, and the stored-order permutations. Mutations, each restored, against cadSketchCurveSymmetry, the equation baseline and the attempt boundaries (41 tests). The equation baseline and the attempt boundaries passed under each. Resetting other mirrors on each retry fails 1, the two-copy test. So do keeping a combination only where the whole sketch solves, and one mirror per component. Ordering combinations by their sum alone fails 1, the combination test. The old quarter-turn wrap fails 1, the tilt test, and so does orienting the mirror by its drawn direction. Planning mirrors in stored order fails 1, the permutation test, and so does letting every mirror start a shared point. Decided after round 4: a nearly collapsed line was accepted. With Parallel between their mirrors stored after the two copies, the solver receives equations in another order, and one mixed combination met every relation with A about 2.6e-6 mm long, down from 7.6 mm, which the graph check’s degenerate threshold, minimumLengthMm (1e-7), accepts. The curve Symmetric’s collapse guard alone now also counts a mirrored curve as collapsed when its solved length or radius falls below mirrorCollapseRelative (1e-5) of its size before the solve, or below minimumLengthMm, whichever is larger; the graph checks are unchanged. publicNotes.summary: Points, lines, arcs and circles can be made symmetric about any line or axis.
changes: Select two lines, two arcs or two circles with a line or the H or V axis, in any order, and choose Symmetric to mirror them as whole curves.
Mirrored arcs and circles keep one radius, and mirrored lines may run either way.

A free mirror line turns to fit lines kept horizontal and vertical, moving the sketch as little as it can and never moving fixed points, and a mirror that other relations already keep is refused as redundant.
Symmetric marks show on both curves and on the mirror line. Choose Symmetric again with the same selection to remove it.
Equal says why a line cannot be equal to an arc or circle.
publicNotes.compatibility: Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions and controller output are unchanged. Sketches with mirrored curves do not open in older releases.
